stories.headline: Update: Polis requests expedited federal disaster declaration for southwest Colorado flooding
stories.summary:
Gov. Jared Polis on Saturday formally asked President Donald Trump and the Federal Emergency Management Agency for an expedited major disaster declaration. The request covers flooding and debris flows that struck Archuleta and Rio Grande counties from Oct. 22 through Oct. 25. It seeks FEMA Public Assistance support for recovery.

The state estimates the storms caused nearly $27 million in damage, and Polis expects that figure to rise. The governor's office said communities suffered significant losses from record-breaking flooding and mud flows. At the height of the event, more than a thousand people on the Colorado side were evacuated from their homes. The damage to infrastructure is expected to take months to fix, and crews are making temporary repairs in the meantime.

The Federal Highway Administration separately approved the Colorado Department of Transportation's request for emergency relief, including $6.5 million in quick-release funding. That money will allow crews to begin road repairs before winter.

Residents of southern Colorado were also urged to evacuate ahead of a weekend storm forecast to bring heavy rain, snow and more flooding. Pagosa Springs issued a mandatory evacuation order Saturday evening for flood-prone areas.

stories.headline: Woman killed after being struck by van in Aurora; man fatally shot in Denver's Clayton neighborhood
stories.summary:
Officials are investigating a deadly crash in Aurora on Thursday evening in which a van allegedly struck a pedestrian. A woman died as a result of the crash. Authorities had not released further details in the report, and the investigation is continuing.

Separately, Denver police are investigating a fatal shooting in the Clayton neighborhood. Officers responded to a shooting call in the 3200 block of East 40th Avenue at about 1:45 a.m. Saturday. They found a man with at least one gunshot wound and took him to a hospital.

Police said in a Saturday afternoon update that the man had died. No arrests have been made. Anyone with information about the shooting or the gunman is asked to contact Crime Stoppers at 720-913-7867.

stories.headline: U.S. Supreme Court to hear Colorado case on religious preschools and public funding
stories.summary:
The U.S. Supreme Court will hear oral arguments Tuesday in St. Mary Catholic Parish v. Roy. The case asks whether religious schools can take public money and still discriminate. It involves two Catholic preschools in the Denver suburbs that declined to join Colorado's state-funded preschool program.

Families of 4-year-olds in the program can choose from dozens of religious preschools alongside hundreds of other options. Participating schools must agree not to discriminate, including on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity. The parishes said admitting gay or transgender children, or children with gay or transgender parents, would conflict with Catholic beliefs, and they sued.

Advocates for Colorado's position warn that a ruling for the preschools could harm children from LGBTQ families and open the door to other exclusions. Patrick Cremin of the Education Law Center said the state would be forced to fund discrimination if the preschools prevail.

Nick Reaves of the Becket Fund for Religious Liberty, which represents the preschools, said harm to LGBTQ families is speculative. He said Colorado's policy has put Catholic families in a bind. Parent plaintiff Lisa Sheley testified that her family would have saved about $4,700 a year had her child's preschool been in the state program. The decision could have implications well beyond Colorado.

stories.headline: Coronado's Ollie Horton breaks own course record for second straight 4A cross-country title
stories.summary:
Coronado senior Ollie Horton won his second consecutive state title Saturday at the Norris Penrose Event Center in Colorado Springs. He finished in 14 minutes, 40.6 seconds, nearly eight seconds faster than his record time from last year. His time was the fastest of the day across all classifications.

Golden's Jackson Ferguson placed second in 14:58.1. Summit's Lucas Remeikis finished third in 15:18.9. Summit won the 4A boys team title with 62 points, ahead of Durango with 81. Coronado, last year's champion, finished third.

In the girls race, Classical Academy won its fourth straight team title and 18th overall. The Titans were moved up to 4A this season by the CHSAA's new success multiplier. Vivian Jack won the individual crown in 17:17.411, and Summit sophomore Kayla Broecker was second. Eaton's Delaney Reuter defended her 3A individual title.

stories.headline: Niwot sweeps 5A titles at Colorado state cross-country championships
stories.summary:
Niwot swept the 5A team championships Saturday at the Norris Penrose Event Center in Colorado Springs. The girls won their seventh title in eight seasons by placing all five scoring runners in the top 15. They scored 47 points, well ahead of runner-up Boulder with 100 and Fairview with 116.

The Niwot boys won their fourth consecutive title and sixth since 2019 with 60 points. Arapahoe was second with 143. Sophomore Jude Ritzenhein finished second individually in 15:11.40, behind Northfield's Abdinasir Hassan, who won in 14:56.50.

Cherokee Trail's Madison Lange won the 5A girls individual title in 17:28, finishing 25.60 seconds ahead of Heritage's Ella McGowan. Josephine Lenart, a Pennsylvania transfer, led Niwot's girls by placing sixth.

stories.headline: Denver Summit FC's playoff hopes come down to NWSL Decision Day
stories.summary:
Denver Summit FC (11-8-10, 41 points) will play at North Carolina on Sunday at 3 p.m., with the final NWSL playoff spot at stake. The match will be shown on ESPN. Denver sits 10th after a 6-1 win over Racing Louisville and is one of three teams still competing for the eighth and last berth.

To advance, the Summit must beat the North Carolina Courage, and Orlando must beat Seattle Reign FC. North Carolina won the teams' last meeting 2-0 on Aug. 5 at Centennial Stadium. Denver leads the league with 53 goals, while North Carolina has 51.

Coach Nick Cushing called it a do-or-die game and said the team would need to be at its best. Forward Yazmeen Ryan said the mentality is that it is effectively the first playoff game. The playoffs begin Nov. 6.

stories.headline: Western Slope vineyards pivot as Colorado wine consumption slumps
stories.summary:
Grand Valley grape growers are leaving fruit on the vines this fall because there is no market for it. Colorado wine sales have dropped 19% since 2020, and consumption is down another 6.2% so far this year. Last year in the Grand Valley's American Viticultural Area, there were no buyers for a third of the roughly 500 acres of grapes.

Industry leaders cite several causes. Baby boomers are drinking less, younger consumers favor canned cocktails, and GLP-1 weight-loss drugs suppress cravings. Health authorities have also declared alcohol unhealthy in any amount. Kyle Schlachter of the Colorado Wine Board said the whole industry is wobbling, and the problem is global.

For three years, more Grand Valley vines have been pulled up than planted. Sauvage Spectrum Estate Winery is discarding bins of unsold Mourvèdre grapes and plans to remove one of five acres of Malbec. Among the valley's 30 wineries, a few are not making wine this year, others are cutting production, and some are keeping vineyards mainly as landscaping. Grande River Vineyards has sold off most of its acreage.

topStory.headline: Alaska Asks Federal Judge to Dismiss Justice Department Suit Seeking to Block Certification of Senate Race
topStory.summary:
Alaska's Republican-led state government on Saturday urged a federal judge to dismiss with prejudice a Justice Department lawsuit that seeks to halt certification of the state's U.S. Senate race if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses. In a filing from the state attorney general's office, which is headed by Republican acting Attorney General Cori Mills, officials wrote that there was "no reason for this Court to entertain this meritless lawsuit any longer." They added that the relief sought is "inappropriate and not even possible given Alaskan voters' vital right to ballot secrecy." The filing came three days before Election Day.

The Justice Department filed the suit Oct. 22 against local election officials at President Donald Trump's direction. It alleges that the campaign of Democratic candidate Mary Peltola helped recruit a second candidate named Dan Sullivan, a retired schoolteacher from Petersburg, creating voter confusion that would siphon votes from the incumbent. The administration amended its complaint this week to cite a New York Times report that texts and posts appeared to show Peltola's campaign was involved in the recruitment and that Peltola was aware of it. The Times story cited a former campaign manager who later tried to retract her statements. Peltola has denied the allegations, telling supporters Friday she was "so deeply offended" by the accusations and did "not need any help" defeating Sullivan. Trump has also demanded that Peltola be prosecuted.

On Friday, the Justice Department added a request that the court separate all ballots marking votes for the second Sullivan until it can be determined whether voters were misled. Alaska's filing called the proposal "both disturbing and impossible," saying it would be easy to identify which ballots rank Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. no matter how they are stored, and that segregating them would violate voter privacy. State officials also noted that the Alaska Supreme Court approved the second candidate's place on the ballot months ago, and that the ballot distinguishes the two men: the senator is listed as the Republican incumbent, while the other appears as "Daniel J. Sullivan Jr." with no party affiliation.

The administration has argued that a preamble to the 1990s law governing voter registration gives the federal government responsibility for ensuring states maintain the integrity of federal elections, and says it is seeking to prevent fraud. Election law experts have broadly criticized the complaint, and Alaska officials challenged the basis for federal standing, noting that certification is left to the states. The Justice Department has also issued a wave of subpoenas and announced a criminal investigation in the case, as the administration has stepped up its use of legal powers ahead of Tuesday's midterm elections.

U.S. District Judge Sharon L. Gleason set Saturday as the deadline for arguments on whether to dismiss the suit without a hearing and is expected to rule soon. The outcome could determine whether the state proceeds with ballot counting and certification without federal interference in a race that could help decide control of the U.S. Senate.
